title: From one idea to coordinated work

slides.title: From one idea to coordinated work
slides.subtitle: A 90-minute, hands-on GitHub Copilot app workshop using the Book App

slides.title: What makes the app different?
bullets: Separate sessions: run focused tasks in parallel, each in its own worktree.
See the work: keep plans, diffs, terminal output, and browser preview in one session.
Specialize help: use a custom agent for a defined role and a skill for reusable task guidance.
Share state: use a canvas to keep decisions and validation evidence visible beside the work.

bullets: 0–3 min · Explain the goal, public-repo access, and setup checklist.

slides.title: 90-minute hands-on workshop
slides.subtitle: The app is the control room; the Book App is the work

slides.title: GitHub + Copilot: from code to collaboration
rows: Shared repositories, issues, branches, pull requests, and reviews.
Understand code, explore options, draft changes, and create tests.
Take defined tasks; people direct, review, and decide what ships.
Reduce repetitive work while staying accountable for quality.

slides.title: What is the GitHub Copilot app?
bullets: A desktop workspace for working with Copilot agents across software tasks—not just another chat window.
Each session keeps a task's conversation and work together; worktrees can isolate changes.
See and manage work in context: plans, file changes, terminal, browser preview, and canvases.
Coordinate multiple tasks, then inspect the evidence and decide what is ready to share.

slides.title: Skills and agents: guidance meets a focused role
bullets: A skill packages reusable instructions and resources for a task that comes up repeatedly.
Example: book-app-reviewer gives Copilot a consistent checklist for filters, stats, and accessibility.
A custom agent is a named specialist with its own role instructions and selected tools.
Example: Book App Reviewer uses that role to create a read-only checklist; a person still verifies the diff and evidence.

slides.title: The GitHub work loop
rows: State the need and what success looks like.
Make a focused change in an isolated worktree.
Review the diff, checks, and behavior.

slides.title: 90 minutes · the learning path
bullets: 0–10 · Orient in the app, connect GitHub/Copilot concepts, and tour the Book App.
10–20 · Frame Clear filters and its acceptance criteria.
20–32 · Plan Session A; create a read-only review checklist in Session B.
32–42 · Mini-teach: sessions, worktrees, modes, agents, and skills.
42–62 · Implement in one session; finish the checklist in the other.
62–78 · Use a canvas, inspect changes, run checks, and validate in Browser.
78–90 · Compare evidence, debrief, and close.

slides.title: Start with the Book App
rows: Find books by title or author.
Narrow by genre and reading status.
See totals for books currently shown.

items.text: Show the control only when search, genre, or reading status is active
Selecting it resets all three filters to their defaults
The full book list and its reading stats return
Keep the change small; preserve existing behavior and dependencies

slides.title: Show the app, not just chat
bullets: New and project sessions start the right kind of work.
Plan mode lets you review an approach before implementation.
Changes, Terminal, and Browser keep code and evidence in context.
Customize and Canvas manage reusable help and visible work state.

slides.title: Describe → plan → build → prove
rows: State the user need and observable acceptance criteria.
Inspect the approach before allowing implementation.
Implement in an isolated worktree; use a second session for review criteria.
Check the diff, tests, build, browser behavior, and canvas evidence.

items.text: Create Session A from the default branch in a new worktree; name it Clear filters build
Use Plan mode and request a small implementation and validation plan
Check the plan against the criteria; approve only when it fits
Switch to Interactive and ask the agent to implement the approved plan
Do not merge or push during the workshop

slides.title: Hands-on 2 · Reviewer session
bullets: Start Session B in a separate new worktree from the default branch; select Book App Reviewer.
Use the book-app-reviewer skill to produce a read-only acceptance checklist.
Ask it to inspect the existing code and state what must be verified—not to edit or run commands.
Session B is independent; it does not automatically see Session A's uncommitted diff.
Later compare its checklist with Session A's actual change and browser behavior.

slides.title: Mini-teach · Keep the work in context
headers: Why it matters in the app
rows: Describe this task and the outcome you need now.
Ground work in the project files and existing patterns.
Keep task history visible and changes isolated.
Track status, then verify with the diff, tests, and browser.

slides.title: Mini-teach · Canvas as the shared board
bullets: Create or open a compact work board in the session side panel.
Track the feature proposal, Session A implementation, Session B review checklist, and verification evidence.
The canvas makes status visible; it does not replace reviewing the diff or running checks.
Use the board to tell what needs attention without searching a long chat.

items.text: Put acceptance criteria on the canvas; update both session lanes from what actually happened
Inspect Session A's Changes diff; compare it with Session B's checklist
Run npm test -- --run and npm run build in samples/book-app-web
In Browser, test no filters, each active filter, and reset behavior
Record only checks you personally observed; mark blocked checks as not run

slides.title: Validate Clear filters
rows: Control hidden; full list and stats show.
All filters reset; full list and stats return.
Tests and build pass; inspect actual output.

slides.title: Compare the evidence
bullets: Session A · What files changed? Does the diff match the plan? Did tests and build pass?
Session B · What criteria did the reviewer identify? Which are confirmed in code?
Browser · What behavior did you personally observe?
Canvas · Does the board reflect actual status, including anything not run?

slides.title: Takeaways
bullets: The app is a place to coordinate work, not only ask for code.
Separate sessions make concurrent tasks visible and isolated.
Skills and custom agents shape how help is delivered; they are not proof of correctness.
A canvas keeps status visible; people still inspect diffs and evidence.
